concept: Exploratory data analysis (EDA) checks distributions, missingness, outliers, and relationships before drawing conclusions or fitting models.
example:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
df = pd.DataFrame({"revenue": [100, 120, 140, 160, 1000]})
print(df["revenue"].describe())
print(df.isna().sum())
df["revenue"].hist(bins=5)
plt.xlabel("Revenue")
plt.show()
breakdown: describe reports summary statistics, including median and quartiles.
isna().sum() counts missing values per column.
The histogram shows the shape of the distribution.
The 1000 value warrants investigation; it is not automatically an error.
practice: Calculate the median and mean revenue and explain which is more affected by the high value.
answer:
print(df["revenue"].median())  # 140.0
print(df["revenue"].mean())    # 304.0
# The mean is pulled upward by 1000; the median is more robust.
takeaways: Inspect distributions before relying on averages.
Do not delete outliers without domain justification.
